title: Building the World's Most Trusted Driver

reader_summary.headline: Hello, everyone, welcome back to the A16C podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hello, everyone, welcome back to the A16C podcast. Now, one of my favorite podcasts we've recorded since I joined the team was just about this time last year. That episode was on autonomous vehicles, but it was actually also in an autonomous vehicle.

key_points.text: That was my first ride in a self-driving car.
key_points.evidence_quote: That was my first ride in a self-driving car.
And over the last year, I've seen so many others have their first as Waymo has expanded to the public in Phoenix and San Francisco, while also placing its roots in Austin and L.A.

key_points.text: In 2015, Waymo tested its first fully driverless ride on public roads.
key_points.evidence_quote: In 2015, Waymo tested its first fully driverless ride on public roads.

key_points.text: It then opened to the public in Phoenix in 2020, but it wasn't until 2022 that autonomous drives were offered in San Francisco.
key_points.evidence_quote: It then opened to the public in Phoenix in 2020, but it wasn't until 2022 that autonomous drives were offered in San Francisco.

thesis: The episode provides an update on the autonomous vehicle industry, highlighting Waymo's expansion to public roads in Phoenix and San Francisco and its achievement of over 7 million driverless miles by the end of 2023. The conversation features Dmitri Dolgov, co-CEO of Waymo, who discusses the history of the field from the 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge to the present, noting that while sensor types remain similar, the underlying AI and computing capabilities have changed drastically since 2007.
